notes.title: Spring Mini-Game Event
notes.notes:
[IMG]http://i.imgur.com/qubXaPH.jpg[/IMG]

[url=https://forum.villagersandheroes.com/showthread.php?8821-Fr%FChlings-Mini-Game-Event] [IMG]http://i.imgur.com/Mzd70Ou.jpg[/IMG]	 [/url]


Have you ever been in this situation?

    You’re staring deep into your vaults, have been for hours, but see only the same old tedious hats and helms, and dusty robes and armors that have been hanging there for too many seasons to count. All around you it’s springtime -- new sights, sounds, and colors abound. But not in your vault, which is as sparkly as a gloomy Pyrron dungeon.

    You happen to catch sight of your reflection -- wrinkled tunic, faded boots, droopy belt -- and your mood improves not at all. For the hundredth time, you wearily think it again: I simply have NOTHING to wear.

    Well, cheer up. We can help you. The legendary fashion designer himself, Adamo Otteramo, recently traveled these parts and left behind, in the hands of his most trusted tailors and seamstresses, the latest creations from his dazzling new spring collection. But it is Adamo’s wish that these rare outfits, divinely elegant, be given to those only worthy enough to wear such finery.

    Adamo values intellect and adventurous spirit. As such, he has instructed his assistants to hide themselves in remote locations throughout the land, exceedingly unusual spots that only the bravest of explorers will ever have a hope of finding. Adamo’s assistants, once located, will then test the explorers further, by asking them a single riddle pertaining to this mystical land in which we all dwell.

    But beware! Adamo loathes multiple choice, nor is he partial to the policy of unlimited guesses. However, as a fashion designer he does understand that it would be unfair if his garments came in only one size, which is why he has given three outfits, of different sizes, to his assistants: Small (levels 1-20), Medium (levels 21-40), and Large (levels 41-70.) The explorers then should seek out those parts of the land most befitting of their size.

    The first explorer to correctly answer the riddle in their level bracket will win Adamo’s latest fashion creation! (Each of the three level brackets will have a different riddle.) There will be three winners on every server, unless of course a riddle goes unsolved. In that case, none may claim that particular garment. (Adamo feels strongly about this.)

  [h1]  Event Details and Rules[/h1]

  [b]  • At the given time, all participating players will congregate in Ardent. A ‘tournament guide’ will then make an announcement:[/b]

  [i]  * Players of levels 1-20 will be given the name of the specific zone in which to look for Adamo’s hidden assistant.
    * Players of levels 21-40 will be given the name of the specific zone in which to look for Adamo’s hidden assistant.
    * Players of levels 41-70 will be given the name of the specific zone in which to look for Adamo’s hidden assistant.[/i]

   [b] • When the names of the three zones have all been revealed, a time clock will be set for one hour. Players will travel to their designated zones and search for the hidden assistants.

    • Adamo’s three assistants will be clearly labeled, so there will be no confusing them with other players.

    • Once a player has found Adamo’s hidden assistant, the following procedure will take place:[/b]

  [i]  * Adamo’s assistant will first verify that the player is in the appropriate zone for their level. If so, the assistant will then invite the player into a private party chat line.
    * The assistant will tell the player the riddle, but will supply them with no other information. (No hints, no clues, nothing.)
    * The player will then be removed from the private party chat line, and can deliberate on the riddle for however long they like. But remember, the clock is ticking!
    * When player is ready to make their guess, they will return to Adamo’s assistant. Player will then invite the assistant into a private party chat line, and make their guess.
    * Player is only allowed one opportunity to guess and the spelling of the answer must be correct. There are no second chances.
    * If player answers the riddle correctly, they will be deemed the winner of the prize, and that particular section level of the tournament, from then on, will be closed.
    * An announcement will be posted on the forums, alerting all players to this. The tournament guide in Ardent will also announce whenever a riddle has been solved.
    * Once a section has been closed, that assistant will then position themselves near the portal of the zone, and routinely announce that the section is now closed.[/i]

   [b] • When the hour is up, the mini-game event is over and no more prizes will be handed out, at all.

    • WHISPERING IS NOT ALLOWED. (We are using the honor system and hope you will abide by it.)

    • Players may only claim prizes that are in their level bracket. For example, a level 50 player may not participate in the level 1-20 section of the tournament.

    • The use of alts is allowed, provided the alt is appropriate to the level bracket. For example, if your main toon answers a riddle incorrectly, you may try for other sections of the tournament with your alt. OR, if your alt happens to be of the same level as your main, you do have an opportunity to make a second guess at the same riddle.

    • On each server, all of Adamo’s assistants will be hidden in the exact same location, and will ask the exact same riddle.

    • The tournament guide in Ardent will be on hand to provide updates, or direct late players to their appropriate level zones, or answer any questions regarding the rules of the event. However, the guide in Ardent will not repeat riddles. Only Adamo’s assistants will ask the riddles, and will repeat them to players as needed.

    • If a player has inadvertently gone to the wrong zone bracket and asks for the riddle, Adamo’s assistant will direct them to the appropriate zone.[/b]

  [h1]  This mini-game event will take place on Sunday, May 25. The start time is:[/h1]

  [b]  • Germany – 7pm (CEST)
    • UK – 6pm (BST)
    • US -- 10am (PDT) 1pm (EDT)
    • Brazil – 2pm (BRT)[/b]

  [i]  Please visit this link to find your exact time zone for the event: [url=http://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/converted.html?iso=20140525T10&p1=816&p2=179&p3=37&p4=136&p5=213] Here [/url][/i]

    There are many who do not visit the forums regularly, so please tell all your friends and guild mates about the event via in-game email.

    Good luck, and hope to see you all there!

    • The use of alts is allowed, provided the alt is appropriate to the level bracket. For example, if your main toon answers a riddle incorrectly, you may try for other sections of the tournament with your alt. OR, if your alt happens to be of the same level as your main, you do have an opportunity to make a second guess at the same riddle.

    • On each server, all of Adamo’s assistants will be hidden in the exact same location, and will ask the exact same riddle.

    • The tournament guide in Ardent will be on hand to provide updates, or direct late players to their appropriate level zones, or answer any questions regarding the rules of the event. However, the guide in Ardent will not repeat riddles. Only Adamo’s assistants will ask the riddles, and will repeat them to players as needed.

    • If a player has inadvertently gone to the wrong zone bracket and asks for the riddle, Adamo’s assistant will direct them to the appropriate zone.[/b]

    • UK – 6pm (BST)
    • US -- 10am (PDT) 1pm (EDT)

notes.title: Release Notes for 2.27.3
notes.notes:
[h1]Notes to the Players[/h1] 
This build is a response to all the player comments. Briefly, the major fixes are:
[list]
[*]Summer’s Hollow and Oak Valley were made more interesting and unique, and include some special challenges and easter eggs.
[*]We improved the controls for movement, the camera, and combat to be snappier and more responsive. But, we're just getting started! More to come.
[*]Multiple players can now use the same crafting station.
[*]We added VSynch.
[/list]

We did not make the changes to Energy yet, but the change will come in the next build.

Stay tuned-- lots more great stuff in the coming weeks. 

[h1]Improvements[/h1] 
[list]
[*]Summer's Hollow and Oak Valley were completely reworked: new monsters (Goblins and Felcats instead of wolves), new and more interesting Quest dialog that matches the quirky and funny style of the game, and other secret stuff…
[*]Improvements to movement and camera control
[list]
[*]We improved the walking, running, and strafing animations.
[*]A & D keys strafe while the right mouse button is held down.
[*]Click-to-move now defaults to off.
[*]Right mouse button no longer causes the character to change direction except while moving with WASD or mouse-drive.
[*]Right mouse button no longer breaks auto-run.
[*]Rotation to a target or move location is now instant and doesn't prevent attacks.
[*]Don't accelerate or decelerate during click-to-move or moving towards target, and reduce over-running.
[*]WASD is now more sensitive and now has a "ramp up" time, instead of immediately moving at full speed.
[/list]
[*]Combat Improvements
[list]
[*]Fixed: The player effect bar sometimes 'blinks' out.
[*]Effect icons now will appear instantly.
[*]Fixed: when switching targets, the effect bar sometimes carries over for upwards of 3-5 seconds.
[*]Feat/Spell Button flash is much shorter now.
[*]Fixed a bug causing effect icons to occasionally briefly disappear.
[*]Combat bar now pops up instantly if combat starts or a feat is used.
[*]Cameo orb of players and NPCs now appears instantly instead of after a few second's delay.
[/list]
[*]We renamed "Sheep Pen" to "Animal Pen"
[*]We added support for Vertical Sync. There is now an option in Settings->Display->Miscellaneous Options->Vertical Sync to turn it on.
[*]We cleaned up Sapphira's Lament, reducing some of the thicker populations of mobs
[*]Belts and gloves now have unique 3d loot objects
[*]The depths got a slight cosmetic touch up with some new torches
[*]The warrior spell Huzzah was cosmetically improved to no longer show green
[*]Enemy Hill Giants bash spell had its damage slightly reduced and its duration reduced.
[*]The "Display" tab in Settings has been renamed "Options" to better match.
[*]There is now a button to send bug reports in the "Display" tab in Settings.
[*]Players who are inactive for 30 minutes will be exited to the Character Select screen.
[*]We removed "Marty" in Ardent who was using the anvil (and taking up space!).
[*]We moved Aldispos.
[*]Strength of the Bear buff now has a 3 minute duration
[*]In-game spirit essence models are now disabled by default.
[*]House Rent: make it so that if the player's account is less than 1 week old, they can rent for 5 days, and prepay for up to 5 days from the current day at any time during that week. If account is 1-2 weeks old, it's 10 days. After 2 weeks, it's like it was before...up to a month prepay, and 2 weeks on purchase. Also there is no foreclosure grace period until 2 weeks.
[*]Multiple characters can now craft at the same anvil, cooking pot, or other crafting node.
[*]Settings changes should no longer be lost when the game crashes.
[*]We Increased XP tables from level 1-10 slightly so players don’t level up so quickly
[*]We removed the series of leveling gift bags and have replaced them with small named gift packs that certain NPCs in Oak Valley give to players. In general players get about the same amount of goods, but they get them at better times rather than all at the end.
[*]All elder parts now have a unique 3D icon to show what they are (instead of the old pyramids)
[*]When Arcron performs an elder restoration, there is now a fancy lightshow.
[*]Charters of all levels now give Charter Tokens 
[*]We made several lighting fixes in Pyrron zones
[*]We tweaked some of the sizes of the monster part 3d loot.
[*]The following negative effects are now curable by the priests cure spell: Confuse, Bewildering Blast, Spore Cloud, Spore Blast, Condemn, Malevolent Roots, Shadow Howl, Frightful Bite, Fear, Paralyzing Fear, Chilling Cry, Doom
[*]Players can now walk beneath Pyrrus legs in Pyrron Courtyard. 
[/list]

[h1] Bugs Fixed[/h1] 
[list]
[*]Fixed: Some Steam Players can't buy crowns. We need to detect if the user does not have the overlay turned on, and if so, post a pop-up to explain what they need to do to enable the Steam Overlay, as well as redirect to the Steam website to complete the purchase.
[*]We fixed a bug causing strafing and moving backwards to sometimes start off not matching camera direction.
[*]Fixed: You are at -52 -253 68 in Shadow Fated Vega, The water is transparent in this location.
[*]Fixed: Level 70 Decoction - making 1 level 70 decoction requires 3 level 65 decoctions and 1 water.
[*]Fixed: We added some tech to hopefully speed up frame rate in The undercroft.
[*]Fixed a bug that was causing Venom of the Serpent to not look correct when cast.
[*]We fixed a bug that caused warrior mobs who cast Huzzah to not be able to attack
[*]We fixed a bug causing signs to show nothing.
[*]The game will now repair itself if it detects it has been corrupted.
[*]We fixed a bug causing the game to freeze while sending a bug report (ironic, we know!)
[/list]

[h1] The following bugs were hot-fixed last week[/h1] 
[list]
[*]We fixed a bug preventing guild players from getting a house in their guild village.
[*]Exception typo: server grabbing prefs from db
[*]Fixed a bug with the Quest log that made it not work for some people at the start of the game.
[*]We Reduced the respawn times of monsters in the first two zones.
[*]We balanced the early zones with more channels so they can accommodate a larger influx of players
[*]We fixed a crash bug caused by some assets not being properly unzipped. This was the second most common crash bug. This would cause the game to crash when launching.
[*]We improved patcher/launcher download rates. It should no longer be too slow to download.
[*]We fixed a bug that prevented certain Brazilian players from signing in from Steam.
[*]We fixed a very rare bug that caused DLC items to sometimes not be granted immediately. NOTE: Players who did not get their items initially will automatically receive them now.
[/list]

[h1] Bugs We Cannot Reproduce (or we need more information)[/h1] 
[list]
[*]“Having problems with showing Cheery the signet from Shangri. It won't work either having ring in bag or on me. The dialogue box does not change either way. Plz could you help.”
[*]“Vega not giving xp for players within 10 lvls only for 5 lvls”
[/list]

notes.title: Housing Shortage Solution
notes.notes:
(German translation below / deutsche Übersetzung im Anschluss)

Hello Everyone,

There is a major housing shortage now (on all of the servers).  We had way more players joining over the last week than we ever imagined. This is a good problem.

However it is causing problems for all of you who want a house.  So, we have come up with a quick solution to free up some houses.  The idea is that people who showed up on the first two days of Steam Launch, got a house, and then never returned--the rent on their houses will expire early.

Precisely Stated: For all players who a) Signed up on April 17 or 18, AND b) have not played since April 20, AND c) have a house, we will set their rent to expire in 24 hours from now (so at about Sunday 8pm Pacific Time).  If you want to keep your house but you haven't played in a week, log on tomorrow, and pay rent.  We won't set it to expire again.  

For those of you who have played the game at least once in the last week, don't worry! :)  Your rent will not expire early.  

We think this will free up over 100 houses on each server.

Thanks!
Damon

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[IMG]http://i.imgur.com/UDP3BK0.png[/IMG] Hallo zusammen,

Momentan gibt es auf allen Servern viel zu wenig Hausplätze. In der letzten Woche haben viel mehr Spieler unser Spiel ausprobiert, als wir jemals erwartet haben. Das ist eigentlich ein sehr positives Problem.

Allerdings bedeutet das auch Probleme für alle die von Euch, die ein Haus bauen möchten. Deswegen sind wir auf die folgende schnelle Lösung gekommen, um ein paar Hausplätze freizugeben. Unsere Idee ist, dass wir alle Häuser von Spielern, die in den ersten beiden Tagen eingeloggt und ein Haus gebaut, dann aber nie mehr eingeloggt haben, schneller freigeben als normal.

Die genaue Lösung sieht wie folgt aus: 

Bei allen Spielern die

Am 17. oder 18. April einen Account angelegt haben
Seit dem 20. April nicht mehr eingeloggt haben
Und ein Haus haben

haben wir die Miete verkürzt und sie am Montag um 5 Uhr enden lassen. Wenn Ihr also zu diesen Spielern gehört und Euer Haus behalten möchtet, dann loggt Euch bitte ein und verlängert Eure Miete. Dieses ist eine einmalige Maßnahme und wir werden dieses Vorgang nicht wiederholen.

Alle die, die in der letzten Woche mindestens einmal eingeloggt haben, ändert sich nichts. Eure Miete wird zur normalen Zeit auslaufen.

Wir glauben, dass dieses Vorgehen bis zu 100 Häuser pro Server freigeben wird.

Danke.
Damon

notes.title: Dev Diary: Combat, Movement, Camera Design Iteration
notes.notes:
[url=https://forum.villagersandheroes.com/showthread.php?8565-Dev-Diary-Geplante-%C4nderungen-an-Kampf-Bewegung-und-Kamera](German translation here / deutsche Übersetzung hier[/url]

Hello Everyone,

Many players have requested we make the combat, movement, and camera snappier and cleaner.  This is a short post of our raw design docs of how we're planning to improve these things.

Again, this is raw design-- we don't spend a lot of time making it pretty, just making sure it's clear.  Feel free to offer advice and comment.
Thanks!

[h1]Click to Move[/h1]
Default this to OFF for new players.

[h1]WASD Sensitivity[/h1]
When the player presses one of the WASD keys, it should accelerate the player's rotational or translational speed over a period of time until it reaches max. I don't think we need a slider for this. It should take about 0.5 seconds to reach max (we can tweak this). This will allow players to tap a key to make small adjustments to direction or position. That's the main goal-- to allow players to have finer control.

[h1]Right Mouse Button[/h1]
Right Mouse Button should no longer control the avatar's direction when the player is not moving. Instead, it should work just like LMB--it controls the camera's direction. Of course, this means that when the player starts to move forward, they will move in the direction of the camera because that is already how it works.

When the player is moving, then yes, the RMB will still control the avatar's direction.

A great side effect of this is that RMB rotate will no longer cancel auto-attack.

[h1]Auto-Run[/h1]
When the player has Auto-Run activated (when Num Lock is held), then RMB+mouse should control direction, and LMB+mouse should pan camera.

[h1]Forward Strafe (aka, Diagonal Strafe)[/h1]
Basically, do a simple fix for this so that when the player does a diagonal strafe (ex: press W + E), then the avatar turns to face in the direction he or she is running, but the camera does not move to be directly behind the avatar. In other words, the camera should still behave as if the character is not rotated in the direction he is running.  This is to avoid the rather silly sliding sideways animation currently in the game. :)

Importantly, when the player stops, the avatar would of course snap back to face the direction he or she was going before doing the diagonal strafe.

Another point: the avatar should move at the same speed as when he is moving forward normally. So, neither faster, nor slower.

Also, the angle currently for diagonal strafe is a little too high. Try it with 30 degrees for now. (And also, make it a set angle. Now I think the angle might change based on various run boosts).

Finally, the head should turn to face in the same direction as the camera (not at the camera-- but in the same direction the camera is facing).

[h1]Combat Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]RMB (above) change will have the advantage of no longer causing accidentally aborted combat.
[*]When the player initiates combat (regardless of how-- auto-attack, etc.), the avatar should instantly snap its rotation to face directly at the enemy.
[*]When the player initiates combat, and the avatar runs to get into range of the target, it should run at full speed, and not decelerate as it nears the target. Therefore, make it stop instantly when reaching attacking distance. Currently it fumbles around with acceleration, rotation, and deceleration creating a non-snappy, sluggish feeling.
[/list]

[h1]Quicker Feedback for Player Action[/h1]
[list]
[*]When the player selects a target, it can take up to a second before the cameo pops up. It would be nice if it popped up immediately. I don't know if any of that info is already sitting on the client (it seems that name, 3d model, and health are already on the client), but if so, we could pop the cameo instantly with this partial information.
[*]The feat/spell icon animation when activating takes too long. It does a shrink and grow and plays a white burst. It should be a quick flash, almost instant, and probably not pulse in size. The goal is to have quick punctuated feedback that the system recognized the user's action.
[*]When the player selects or targets an enemy, and the feat bar pops up--instead of having it slide up, make it instantly pop up. We can still use the slide effect for making it go away and when the player mouses over it to bring it up.
[/list]

[h1]Iteration #2[/h1]
[b]Auto-Select[/b]
When the player does not have any target, then feat & spell icons should be lit (currently, offensive spells/feats will only light up when a target is selected). The player can still try to cast the feat or spell. When they do, the game will try to pick a valid target:
[list]
[*]the game tries to pick out a valid target for the spell or feat. Obviously, it should be an enemy for an offensive spell. Then it picks the nearest valid target that is in front of the player within a reasonable range. If there are none, it will consider enemies that are behind the player.
[*]If it finds a valid target, then that target is selected (cameo pops up), the spell or feat is targeted at that enemy, and that enemy will now be auto-attacked.
[*]If it does not find a valid target, the game will play the animation for the feat or spell, but it will stop without firing a missile, etc. and no spirit will be deducted.
[/list]


[b]Move & Attack[/b]
When a player first clicks on an enemy to attack it (either with auto-attack or with an offensive spell), then the player's avatar will engage the enemy (just like now). By this, I mean the player will snap to face the target and move to be within range. That's the same as now.

Here's the change: the player should still be allowed to move around, and this will not cancel auto-attack, or even a spell or feat in progress. HOWEVER, if the player moves so the target is out of range, or so the target is not within the +/- 30 degree cone of the player, then the attack or feat/spell will not fire off. However, auto-attack is not cancelled, so that, if the player's target becomes valid again, the auto-attack would resume.

Basically, do a simple fix for this so that when the player does a diagonal strafe (ex: press W + E), then the avatar turns to face in the direction he or she is running, but the camera does not move to be directly behind the avatar. In other words, the camera should still behave as if the character is not rotated in the direction he is running.  This is to avoid the rather silly sliding sideways animation currently in the game. :)

Importantly, when the player stops, the avatar would of course snap back to face the direction he or she was going before doing the diagonal strafe.

Another point: the avatar should move at the same speed as when he is moving forward normally. So, neither faster, nor slower.

Also, the angle currently for diagonal strafe is a little too high. Try it with 30 degrees for now. (And also, make it a set angle. Now I think the angle might change based on various run boosts).

Finally, the head should turn to face in the same direction as the camera (not at the camera-- but in the same direction the camera is facing).

[h1]Combat Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]RMB (above) change will have the advantage of no longer causing accidentally aborted combat.
[*]When the player initiates combat (regardless of how-- auto-attack, etc.), the avatar should instantly snap its rotation to face directly at the enemy.
[*]When the player initiates combat, and the avatar runs to get into range of the target, it should run at full speed, and not decelerate as it nears the target. Therefore, make it stop instantly when reaching attacking distance. Currently it fumbles around with acceleration, rotation, and deceleration creating a non-snappy, sluggish feeling.
[/list]

[h1]Quicker Feedback for Player Action[/h1]
[list]
[*]When the player selects a target, it can take up to a second before the cameo pops up. It would be nice if it popped up immediately. I don't know if any of that info is already sitting on the client (it seems that name, 3d model, and health are already on the client), but if so, we could pop the cameo instantly with this partial information.
[*]The feat/spell icon animation when activating takes too long. It does a shrink and grow and plays a white burst. It should be a quick flash, almost instant, and probably not pulse in size. The goal is to have quick punctuated feedback that the system recognized the user's action.
[*]When the player selects or targets an enemy, and the feat bar pops up--instead of having it slide up, make it instantly pop up. We can still use the slide effect for making it go away and when the player mouses over it to bring it up.
[/list]

[h1]Iteration #2[/h1]
[b]Auto-Select[/b]
When the player does not have any target, then feat & spell icons should be lit (currently, offensive spells/feats will only light up when a target is selected). The player can still try to cast the feat or spell. When they do, the game will try to pick a valid target:
[list]
[*]the game tries to pick out a valid target for the spell or feat. Obviously, it should be an enemy for an offensive spell. Then it picks the nearest valid target that is in front of the player within a reasonable range. If there are none, it will consider enemies that are behind the player.
[*]If it finds a valid target, then that target is selected (cameo pops up), the spell or feat is targeted at that enemy, and that enemy will now be auto-attacked.
[*]If it does not find a valid target, the game will play the animation for the feat or spell, but it will stop without firing a missile, etc. and no spirit will be deducted.
[/list]


[b]Move & Attack[/b]
When a player first clicks on an enemy to attack it (either with auto-attack or with an offensive spell), then the player's avatar will engage the enemy (just like now). By this, I mean the player will snap to face the target and move to be within range. That's the same as now.

Here's the change: the player should still be allowed to move around, and this will not cancel auto-attack, or even a spell or feat in progress. HOWEVER, if the player moves so the target is out of range, or so the target is not within the +/- 30 degree cone of the player, then the attack or feat/spell will not fire off. However, auto-attack is not cancelled, so that, if the player's target becomes valid again, the auto-attack would resume.

notes.title: Fan Writing Contest
notes.notes:
[url=https://forum.villagersandheroes.com/showthread.php?8506-Fan-Writing-Contest](German translation here / deutsche Übersetzung hier)[/url]

Hi, everyone! We know how creative you all are, so here is another opportunity to let your imaginations run wild. This time we’re asking for a fictional story, no more than two pages. We will supply the topic, as well as five random elements which, in some way, however you choose, must all be worked into the story. 

The story topic is: A strange spell has lately infected Memorial Pond, causing all of the inhabitants in the area to……

[b]The five elements are:[/b]

[i]1) A cave brute suffering from acute bog frog-a-phobia
2) A loom
3) A troupe of oddly dancing Fire Wizards
4) Jupty Pies
5) An overworked auctioneer from AH vacationing in the countryside, OR an existing in-game NPC[/i]

This contest is designed simply to be fun, so please do not worry about trying to craft beautiful Shakespearean prose, or using perfect MLA writing format standards, etc. You are being judged purely on originality. The form your story takes is entirely up to you – so whether it’s written in third person, first person, stream of consciousness, whatever, it’s completely your choice how you wish to convey the material. 

It can be anywhere from one paragraph to two pages in length, but just please make sure to give your story a title. (Feel free, also, to write about your guild if you wish, or any inventive back stories or bounty runs you and your mates might have gone on. In other words, the sky’s the limit here.)

Submissions will be anonymous! We ask that you send us your story privately, and then we will post it without your name onto the V&H forums, as well as onto the Steam page. The Mad Otter developers will select their top five favorite stories, at which point all of you players will vote on Steam for the top three winning stories, but will have no idea who wrote them. Once the winners have been determined, the names of all the writers will then be re-attached to their respective stories. However, if you would prefer to remain anonymous throughout, please just let us know that when submitting your entry.

This contest is open to players in every country, so please participate in which every language you are most comfortable writing in. We would ask, though, that you also include a Google Translation or equivalent with your submission, but you will not be judged upon the mechanics of that version, simply upon content and creativity. (And both versions will be posted.)

Please send your submissions to: fansubmission@madottergames.com

Deadline is May 2nd, 2014

Contest winners will receive:

[b]1st Place Winner = [/b]A signed 8.5” x 11” picture of in game scenery, a special in game hat, and 250 crowns.

[b]2nd Place Winner =[/b] A special in game hat, and 250 crowns.

[b]3rd Place Winner = [/b]250 crowns

[b]4th Place Winner = [/b]100 crowns

[b]5th Place Winner = [/b]100 crowns

Submit your story to here  fansubmission@madottergames.com

Good luck and have fun!

notes.title: Day Four Feedback: We are Listening
notes.notes:
[url=https://forum.villagersandheroes.com/showthread.php?8440-Tag-4-Steam-Feedback-Wir-h%F6ren-Euch-zu!&p=70086#post70086](German translation here / deutsche Übersetzung hier)[/url]

Hello Players!

Villagers and Heroes has been live on Steam now for nearly 4 days.  Wow! Steam really brings the players.  We are so excited to be on the biggest game portal in the world.

We have received a lot of great advice from all of you on how we can make the game better.  We know that a community of players is the best way to steer the direction of the the game.  It’s the players that bring the game to life.  We are listening.

There are now a ton of things we want to improve and fix.  We want to go as fast as possible, so we want to get a quick build out asap to demonstrate we are listening.

So, the quick build will include some or all of these things:
[list]
[*]A & D keys will strafe (instead of rotate) when the player is moving forwards or backwards with the mouse
[*]We will improve the sideways/strafe animation
[*]We will add a dancing animation! (more to come later)
[*]We’ll make the tutorial do a better job of setting the mood of the game, offer more of a challenge, and have some hidden side areas to explore.
[*]We’re going to improve chat to make it easier to use
[*]We’re going to make the UI a little easier to friend and party up with other players.
[*]Moving will not cancel auto-attack--players need to be able to move around while attacking
[/list]

There are some major bugs we are working on.  The two biggest are: 1. Some players can’t launch the game from Steam.  When they do, nothing happens!  We really want to get this fixed.  We will be contacting some of these players for more information to help us debug the problem.  2. Frequent crash bugs for some players.  Some players are reporting they crash about once every 30 minutes.  Again, we’ll be delving into this.

We do want to apologize also for some of the players getting stuck.  We had to reboot the servers a few times.  These are typical growing pains when you get a huge influx of new players.  This puts extra strain on the servers, and exposes problems we were unaware of.  We’ve fixed many of the problems we found. The game should become more and more stable over time.

And, to our Brazilian players, we are trying to figure out why some of you cannot run or login to the game. Please remain patient.  When we have a fix, we will make an announcement.

Most of all, thanks for all the advice!  Please keep letting us know how to improve the game.

Best Regards,
Damon

p.s. Many of these things were discussed by Diet in an earlier announcement: http://steamcommunity.com/games/263540/announcements/detail/1801747291772990218
I just wanted to give you an update after 4 days.

notes.title: Villagers and Heroes: A Place Where Women Can Be Themselves
notes.notes:
[url=https://forum.villagersandheroes.com/showthread.php?8438-Dev-Diary-Villagers-and-Heroes-Ein-Ort-an-dem-Frauen-ganz-sie-selbst-sein-k%F6nnen&p=70081#post70081](German translation here / deutsche Übersetzung hier)[/url]

[IMG]http://i.imgur.com/eokSMgT.png[/IMG]

If you’re looking for a multiplayer fantasy game in which sorceress babes flounce into combat armed in their ever pragmatic bikinis, or who violently hack and slash away at their friends in a gore filled frenzy of carnage, or who titter inanely in the background doing nothing at all, then best don’t read on because Villagers and Heroes is, refreshingly, not that game. 

Welcome to a land you’ll never want to leave – it’s a place where women wear clothes and debate the statistics of ice javelin damage ratios instead of bosom dimensions; where they coordinate community projects as opposed to raiding their neighbors’ crops, and where, instead of slaughtering each other, they thrillingly battle, in strategic coordination with their teammates, all manner of challenging monsters and foes in a surprisingly bloodless fashion.  

Villagers and Heroes is a rare gem in today’s gaming world, not simply because of its remarkable lack of sexism and depictions of graphic violence, but rather because of the consequences of those choices – it is a wonderfully civilized group of people who play this game, and it is their personalities, generous, respectful, and intelligent, which have created such a positive environment, one in which women can especially thrive.  And they do.  

Women of all ages, backgrounds, and nationalities have discovered that Villagers and Heroes offers them something that so many other MMOs do not:  a place where they can simply be themselves.  Armed with choices, beginning with an assortment of non-degrading character ‘toons’ to select from, the female players, from the moment they step into this intoxicating world, are free to do, and be, exactly as they please. And whether it’s combat, crafting, questing, or even just organizing vaults for hours on end, they will always be in good company.

So to any and all prospective players out there, please know that a game does exist in which men and women are treated equally.  And perhaps because of this, not only is a great deal of fun had by both sexes and lasting friendships made, but Villagers and Heroes has gathered within its fold a particularly thoughtful and strong-minded group of women.  But don’t take my word for it.  Read for yourselves what they had to say about their experiences in the game, what drew them to it, and just what it is that keeps them playing.
-- Sarah Otter


[i]“I like that I can choose a female character and still be able to take care of myself.” [/i] – Fauna G Windspirit

[i]“It makes this game quite unique.  The complete equality between male and female characters (down to the distribution of male and female NPC and their "jobs"), the lack of gore and exaggerated depictions of violence, the cartoonish but not too childish look, the absolute absence of PvP and competitiveness, but a heavy stress on working together, all the other non-violent activities the game has to offer (gardening etc. And crafting. I hate crafting.) All of this might be appealing to women, and it should be highlighted more, so that women looking for games might give this one a try.” [/i] – Mackiai

[i]“We were not defined or confined by the fact we were playing a female character…I guess you could say, there are no limitations in this game, just because you play a female toon. No preset expectation of what you should or should not be able to accomplish.”[/i] – Soy Azeltin

[i] “I loved the fact that the female "toons" themselves weren't just the "bubbleheaded side-kick" to the warriors I saw in so many other games at that time, the half-dressed buxom toons that were all over the searches. But here they are just as awesome and could hold their own in a fight. That the classes are limited only by the imagination of the player and we aren't led around by the nose and made to do certain tasks at certain times but instead are free to do what we please, when we please, or free to just stand in one place and goof off with friends.”[/i]  – IrishElf

[i]“This is the first game I played that has an actual character that I can see. Being able to pick out my own look is a huge plus.”  [/i]-- Myst

[i] “The one thing I love most about this game is the community! I have played Runescape, World of Warcraft, and many other games over the years. This is the only game I keep coming back to. We are like a family not just in our guilds but in general game play as well. Everyone (give or take) works together as a whole to accomplish things from crafting to bounty hunting. I love that my toon doesn't have a rack the size of a baboons butt, or hips that make hippo's envious.” [/i] –  Trillium

[i]“I never really knew why people went out of their way to help, but having played so long now I have adopted that same nature and continue to pay it forward, hoping that those that I help do the same to continue growing a friendly environment in which players can log on to relax and make friends.” [/i]– Scarlet     

[i]“I LOVE the community here…I've made (and, sadly, lost) too many friends to leave. I've had so many joys and tears with this game....so many memories, parties, etc. I’ve seen many faces come and go.  When they leave, I always tell them I’ll leave the lights on for them.”[/i]   –  DaimTest

[i]“The market is saturated with PvP glorifying games, where even your friends are your enemy; there are also countless 'no-brainer' type games out there, but very few that appeal to the growing number of reasonably mature, credit card wielding women who wish to spend a bit of stress free, quality time on line. So far this game is providing all that.”  [/i]–  Kaydee

[i]“Another thing I truly enjoy is the fact that I can work together with other players if I want to, but when I’m in the mood for a bit more solitude, I can do almost everything on my own as well.  The community on the German server is great, and I was surprised to find out just how many women play V&H, as I was (wrongly - and probably misguided by the media) under the impression that computer games and especially MMOs are more of a “guy thing.”” [/i] – Bluerider 

[i]“I love this game! I've logged on almost every single day since I began playing back in 2012.  But what I like best is the energy that comes from other players. I spend hours standing around in Ardent just chatting, cracking jokes, teasing and flirting, but also lending a sympathetic ear, asking for advice and helping others with questions.”[/i] – Vinalso

[i]“I can’t stop playing and wouldn’t try! I do want to add that there are quite a few of us "older" or more mature female players in here too, I happen to be in my sixties and have never played any other games like this before. A friend kept telling me I should play this game and after a few months I decided to try V&H and haven't looked back! I love the friends I've made, how everyone helps each other.. whether it's crafting or killing those "multi-legged" critters and just the game itself!” [/i]–  Madd Mary

notes.title: Villagers and Heroes: A Place Where Women Can Be Themselves
notes.notes:
[url=https://forum.villagersandheroes.com/showthread.php?8438-Dev-Diary-Villagers-and-Heroes-Ein-Ort-an-dem-Frauen-ganz-sie-selbst-sein-k%F6nnen&p=70081#post70081](German translation here / deutsche Übersetzung hier)[/url]

[IMG]http://i.imgur.com/eokSMgT.png[/IMG]

If you’re looking for a multiplayer fantasy game in which sorceress babes flounce into combat armed in their ever pragmatic bikinis, or who violently hack and slash away at their friends in a gore filled frenzy of carnage, or who titter inanely in the background doing nothing at all, then best don’t read on because Villagers and Heroes is, refreshingly, not that game. 

Welcome to a land you’ll never want to leave – it’s a place where women wear clothes and debate the statistics of ice javelin damage ratios instead of bosom dimensions; where they coordinate community projects as opposed to raiding their neighbors’ crops, and where, instead of slaughtering each other, they thrillingly battle, in strategic coordination with their teammates, all manner of challenging monsters and foes in a surprisingly bloodless fashion.  

Villagers and Heroes is a rare gem in today’s gaming world, not simply because of its remarkable lack of sexism and depictions of graphic violence, but rather because of the consequences of those choices – it is a wonderfully civilized group of people who play this game, and it is their personalities, generous, respectful, and intelligent, which have created such a positive environment, one in which women can especially thrive.  And they do.  

Women of all ages, backgrounds, and nationalities have discovered that Villagers and Heroes offers them something that so many other MMOs do not:  a place where they can simply be themselves.  Armed with choices, beginning with an assortment of non-degrading character ‘toons’ to select from, the female players, from the moment they step into this intoxicating world, are free to do, and be, exactly as they please. And whether it’s combat, crafting, questing, or even just organizing vaults for hours on end, they will always be in good company.

So to any and all prospective players out there, please know that a game does exist in which men and women are treated equally.  And perhaps because of this, not only is a great deal of fun had by both sexes and lasting friendships made, but Villagers and Heroes has gathered within its fold a particularly thoughtful and strong-minded group of women.  But don’t take my word for it.  Read for yourselves what they had to say about their experiences in the game, what drew them to it, and just what it is that keeps them playing.
-- Sarah Otter


[i]“I like that I can choose a female character and still be able to take care of myself.” [/i] – Fauna G Windspirit

[i]“It makes this game quite unique.  The complete equality between male and female characters (down to the distribution of male and female NPC and their "jobs"), the lack of gore and exaggerated depictions of violence, the cartoonish but not too childish look, the absolute absence of PvP and competitiveness, but a heavy stress on working together, all the other non-violent activities the game has to offer (gardening etc. And crafting. I hate crafting.) All of this might be appealing to women, and it should be highlighted more, so that women looking for games might give this one a try.” [/i] – Mackiai

[i]“We were not defined or confined by the fact we were playing a female character…I guess you could say, there are no limitations in this game, just because you play a female toon. No preset expectation of what you should or should not be able to accomplish.”[/i] – Soy Azeltin

[i] “I loved the fact that the female "toons" themselves weren't just the "bubbleheaded side-kick" to the warriors I saw in so many other games at that time, the half-dressed buxom toons that were all over the searches. But here they are just as awesome and could hold their own in a fight. That the classes are limited only by the imagination of the player and we aren't led around by the nose and made to do certain tasks at certain times but instead are free to do what we please, when we please, or free to just stand in one place and goof off with friends.”[/i]  – IrishElf

notes.title: Launch Day Feedback: We are listening!
notes.notes:
([url=https://forum.villagersandheroes.com/showthread.php?8380-Steam-Launch-Feedback&p=69621#post69621]German translation/deutsche Übersetzung)[/url]

One of the great parts about indie development is that there is a very accessible and close connection between developers and players, i.e. we don’t have to go through mounds of paperwork and oodles of meetings to get things done. 

One of the great parts about launching on such a large gaming portal like Steam is that our game is fanned in front of thousands of eyes, and in turn we get some great feedback, all of which is great! If it is a heartfelt thanks, or a crushingly negative review, it is still feedback and it is still great for us to hear. [b][i]We think the best way to make any game great is to have a two way street of communication with players and consider all feedback, even the negative.[/i][/b]

In turn, when you combine the quick turnaround speed that indie development offers, along with all of the great new feedback, it means our game will begin to get buffed and shined, and we will end up with a gem in no time. 

We have been on the forums, Steam chat, YouTube, hanging out in game, reading player reviews, and keeping our ears to the ground everywhere we can think of. 

[h1]We know it’s only been one day, but here is what we have learned so far, and more importantly,[i] here is what we are going to do about it.[/i][/h1]

[list][*][b]Attack While Moving[/b] We have heard several players ask to be able to move and attack at the same time. This requires a bit of tech and new animations to make happen, but we think this would be a move in a positive direction. We have IMMEDIATELY started our artists on this task.

[*][b]Controls[/b]: Several players have made note of both AD strafe (vs QE strafe) as well as the jerkiness of WASD. Again, we agree. We have already fixed for strafe, and will be looking at the WASD issues. These both should be live with our next build. 

[*][b]Animations[/b]: We have received several suggestions that our character animations aren't expressive enough. Some of them feel clunky and out of date, particularly strafing. We agree. Our artists have started working on some new animations to really make our characters feel alive. 

[*][b]Linearity of the starting zones[/b]: While the game does open up quite a bit after level 12-15, a lot of new players noted that the early zones felt very linear with little room for exploration. We agree. We are going to go through each of those zones and add a few secret and optional areas for players to discover. 

[*][b]NPC Greetings[/b]: Our NPC’s greet players in several different languages. This was something that was intentionally done to add some variety to our game world. However many players have felt that this was some sort of localization bug, and others just plain don't like it. We are going to take steps to start cleaning these up to make them feel both more accurate to the server, as well as expressive of the NPC speaking.

[*][b]Launcher Stability[/b]: We have had a lot of players having issues with the launcher either crashing or not launching the game. This will be one of our main priorities to fix. 

[*][b]Dancing[/b]: Several players have asked for dancing animations for their character. It may be a small thing, but we think that would be great, and we have started working on it.[/list]

[h1]Additionally, these are things that we have heard from the community, and have already fixed (these changes are live):[/h1]
[list][*][b]The download was taking too long:[/b] We have fixed this. Our CDN was overloaded so we moved it to Amazon Cloudfront. Reports are that download speed has been increased.

[*][b]Tutorial zones were overwhelmed:[/b] We have opened up more channels and instances in the zones to allow for more new players at one time. 

[*][b]Respawn rates were too low:[/b] We lowered respawn times from 1.5 minutes down to 12 seconds. We will continue to monitor the tutorial zones as well as other high level zones and make tweaks as we need.

[*][b]Quest tracker was broken:[/b] We fixed this.

[*][b]Some new players got a ‘zone full’ message:[/b] We made a way for more tutorial channels to open. No player should see this message again![/list]

We hope you can come along with us on Villagers and Heroes journey. We love live development, and we love working with players of all types. Leave your suggestions on the forums, or send us a PM on Steam. We would love to hear from you. 

-The Mad Otter Team

notes.title: Choosing a Server
notes.notes:
(German translation below / deutsche Übersetzung im Anschluß)

When you first start, the game will pick a server for you.  However, you can choose a different server.  A quick guide:

[b]US:[/b] choose this server if you want help getting started.  This server has been around a while, and is filled with lots of friendly people.

[b]US2:[/b]  choose this server if you want to start in an all-new world that has just been opened!  All characters here will be new.

[b]DE:[/b]  choose this server if you want to play with players in Germany.  Most players here speak German.

[b]UK:[/b]  choose this server if you want to play with players in England.

[b]BR:[/b]  choose this server if you want to play with players in Brazil.  Most players here speak Brazilian-Portuguese.

You are free to play on any or even ALL servers!  However, the characters you create on a server cannot be migrated around to different servers. The reason for the new server is so players can start fresh in a new world.

Thanks!

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[IMG]http://i.imgur.com/UDP3BK0.png[/IMG] [b]Serverauswahl[/b]

Beim ersten Spielstart wird das Spiel Dir einen Server aussuchen. Du kannst selbstverständlich auch auf einem anderen Server spielen:

[b]US:[/b] Wähle diesen Server, wenn Du mit nordamerikanischen Spielern spielen möchtest und nichts gegen Hilfe beim Start hast. Dieser Server existiert bereits eine Weile und auf ihm spielen schon eine Menge netter Leute!

[b]US2:[/b] Wähle diesen Server, wenn Du in einer ganz neuen Welt starten möchtest, die gerade erst geöffnet wurde! Alle Charaktere hier beginnen bei null!

[b]DE:[/b] Wähle diesen Server, wenn Du mit vornehmlich deutschsprachigen Spielern spielen möchtest. Dieser Server existiert bereits eine Weile.

[b]UK:[/b] Wähle diesen Server, wenn du mit vornehmlich englischsprachigen europäischen Spielern spielen möchtest. Dieser Server existiert bereits eine Weile.

[b]BR:[/b]  Wähle diesen Server, wenn du mit vornehmlich brasilianischen Spielern spielen möchtest. Dieser Server existiert bereits eine Weile.

Du kannst frei auswählen, auf welchem Server Du spielen möchtest. Du kannst auch auf mehr als einem Server spielen. Charaktere können allerdings NICHT von einem Server auf einen anderen umziehen. Der Grund für den neuen US Server ist, damit es für Steam Spieler einen Server gibt, auf dem alle gleichzeitig wieder bei null starten.  

Danke!

notes.title: Slaying Ghosts
notes.notes:
[h1]Slaying Ghosts: How we boosted zone load by 5x[/h1]

[URL=https://forum.villagersandheroes.com/showthread.php?8361-Dev-Diary-quot-Geister-t%F6ten-Wie-wir-Zonenladezeiten-um-das-F%FCnffache-verk%FCrzt-haben-quot&p=69437#post69437](German translation / deutsche Übersetzung) [/URL]

In a game like Villagers and Heroes, the game world is refereed by a central server (actually, many).  The central server makes sure all the players see the same thing on their computer.  Its job is to keep all the objects in the world synchronized across everyone’s computer.  

Take a look at this sample screen from the game:

[URL=http://i.imgur.com/z9PC91g.jpg][IMG]http://i.imgur.com/z9PC91g.jpg[/IMG][/URL]

There are many objects in this scene: player avatars, monsters, trees, a lamp post, a road, a river, and so on.  All of those objects must be tracked.  Here’s a schematic drawing of what the server sees:
 
[URL=http://i.imgur.com/Xkyb9cM.jpg][IMG]http://i.imgur.com/Xkyb9cM.jpg[/IMG][/URL]

[h1]I labelled these objects:[/h1]
1. Player Avatar
2. Monster
3. Lamp Post
4. River
5.Tree(s) 
6. Bridge

The server has to make sure that all of these objects are in the exact same place on everyone’s computer.  So, to accomplish this, it transmits over the internet, each object’s type (tree, players, monster, etc.), and its location.

Here’s a new picture that shows this communication taking place between the server and one of the player’s computers.  A player’s computer is often called a client.

[URL=http://i.imgur.com/is435D7.jpg][IMG]http://i.imgur.com/is435D7.jpg[/IMG][/URL]

Every arrow in this diagram represents a transmission that the server must make to ALL the clients in the game (at least to players who are near this location in the world).  (Side Note: There is only one arrow going from the Client back to the Server.  That’s because the only object that the Client has control over is the player’s avatar.)  Each of these arrows is expensive.  Hundreds of bytes must be transmitted per object per client.  This puts Load on the server-- it eats up CPU cycles and chews up Server bandwidth.  The consequence of this is that it can make the game appear “laggy” or sluggish.  And, possibly worse, it can take time for all the information to be transmitted from the server to the client.

The process of transmitting information about objects is called “ghosting”.  Each object in the scene exists in two places-- one on the server, and one on the client.  The copy on the server is considered the real object, and the copy that the server transmitted--or “ghosted”--is considered its ghost.

Finally, I should mention that this picture is simplified.  In a real situation, there are HUNDREDS of objects being ghosted from the server to the client.


[h1]What does the game Tribes have to do with Villagers and Heroes?[/h1]
Now I want to take a brief detour.  The engine that Villagers and Heroes uses is Torque3D.  This a third-generation engine based on the game engine that Dynamix developed for the game “Tribes”.  Tribes is one of the most influential games in game history.  It was the first First Person Shooter game to feature powered battlesuits, team-based matches, and jump jets.  It’s the forerunner of games like HALO and TitanFall.  One area where it excelled was in its networking.  One of the design goals of Tribes was that every mission should be completely moddable.  Along with ability of any player to run their own server, it allowed the community to build their own custom missions.

However, one of the costs of having completely moddable missions, is that the server has to tell every client where everything is (and what everything is).

Look back at the picture that shows ghosting from server to client.  Most of the objects in that picture never move. Of all of those objects, the only objects that DO move are the player, and the monsters.  So, it is a waste that we are transmitting the types and positions of EVERY object in the scene.  A better solution is to have the Client load the types and positions of all the non-moving objects from the hard drive.  It is WAY faster to load from hard drive than receiving the information over the internet.  Additionally, when the player’s computer can handle all this work completely on its own, this saves the server a tremendous amount of work, cutting down on CPU and bandwidth usage.  Here is a schematic of what the new system looks like:

[URL=http://i.imgur.com/P7Khb9M.jpg][IMG]http://i.imgur.com/P7Khb9M.jpg[/IMG][/URL]

This is the system that Clark Fagot implemented for the game recently.  Red arrows increase load times and put load on the server, whereas green arrows load quickly and put no load on the server.


[h1]The Results[/h1]
[b][i]On average, it reduced the zone loading times for our players from 40 seconds to 8 seconds.[/i][/b]  This is the difference between getting bored and keeping the gameplay rolling.  In addition, it saves bandwidth for the game servers, and all the players.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[IMG]http://i.imgur.com/UDP3BK0.png[/IMG] Eine deutsche Übersetzung dieses Artikels findet Ihr in unserem Forum:

[URL=https://forum.villagersandheroes.com/showthread.php?8361-Dev-Diary-quot-Geister-t%F6ten-Wie-wir-Zonenladezeiten-um-das-F%FCnffache-verk%FCrzt-haben-quot&p=69437#post69437]Geister töten, oder wie wir es geschafft haben, die Zonenladezeiten um das Fünffache zu verkürzen. [/URL]

notes.title: Slaying Ghosts
notes.notes:
[h1]Slaying Ghosts: How we boosted zone load by 5x[/h1]

[URL=https://forum.villagersandheroes.com/showthread.php?8361-Dev-Diary-quot-Geister-t%F6ten-Wie-wir-Zonenladezeiten-um-das-F%FCnffache-verk%FCrzt-haben-quot&p=69437#post69437](German translation / deutsche Übersetzung) [/URL]

In a game like Villagers and Heroes, the game world is refereed by a central server (actually, many).  The central server makes sure all the players see the same thing on their computer.  Its job is to keep all the objects in the world synchronized across everyone’s computer.  

Take a look at this sample screen from the game:

[URL=http://i.imgur.com/z9PC91g.jpg][IMG]http://i.imgur.com/z9PC91g.jpg[/IMG][/URL]

There are many objects in this scene: player avatars, monsters, trees, a lamp post, a road, a river, and so on.  All of those objects must be tracked.  Here’s a schematic drawing of what the server sees:
 
[URL=http://i.imgur.com/Xkyb9cM.jpg][IMG]http://i.imgur.com/Xkyb9cM.jpg[/IMG][/URL]

[h1]I labelled these objects:[/h1]
1. Player Avatar
2. Monster
3. Lamp Post
4. River
5.Tree(s) 
6. Bridge

The server has to make sure that all of these objects are in the exact same place on everyone’s computer.  So, to accomplish this, it transmits over the internet, each object’s type (tree, players, monster, etc.), and its location.

Here’s a new picture that shows this communication taking place between the server and one of the player’s computers.  A player’s computer is often called a client.

[URL=http://i.imgur.com/is435D7.jpg][IMG]http://i.imgur.com/is435D7.jpg[/IMG][/URL]

Every arrow in this diagram represents a transmission that the server must make to ALL the clients in the game (at least to players who are near this location in the world).  (Side Note: There is only one arrow going from the Client back to the Server.  That’s because the only object that the Client has control over is the player’s avatar.)  Each of these arrows is expensive.  Hundreds of bytes must be transmitted per object per client.  This puts Load on the server-- it eats up CPU cycles and chews up Server bandwidth.  The consequence of this is that it can make the game appear “laggy” or sluggish.  And, possibly worse, it can take time for all the information to be transmitted from the server to the client.

The process of transmitting information about objects is called “ghosting”.  Each object in the scene exists in two places-- one on the server, and one on the client.  The copy on the server is considered the real object, and the copy that the server transmitted--or “ghosted”--is considered its ghost.

Finally, I should mention that this picture is simplified.  In a real situation, there are HUNDREDS of objects being ghosted from the server to the client.


[h1]What does the game Tribes have to do with Villagers and Heroes?[/h1]
Now I want to take a brief detour.  The engine that Villagers and Heroes uses is Torque3D.  This a third-generation engine based on the game engine that Dynamix developed for the game “Tribes”.  Tribes is one of the most influential games in game history.  It was the first First Person Shooter game to feature powered battlesuits, team-based matches, and jump jets.  It’s the forerunner of games like HALO and TitanFall.  One area where it excelled was in its networking.  One of the design goals of Tribes was that every mission should be completely moddable.  Along with ability of any player to run their own server, it allowed the community to build their own custom missions.

However, one of the costs of having completely moddable missions, is that the server has to tell every client where everything is (and what everything is).

Look back at the picture that shows ghosting from server to client.  Most of the objects in that picture never move. Of all of those objects, the only objects that DO move are the player, and the monsters.  So, it is a waste that we are transmitting the types and positions of EVERY object in the scene.  A better solution is to have the Client load the types and positions of all the non-moving objects from the hard drive.  It is WAY faster to load from hard drive than receiving the information over the internet.  Additionally, when the player’s computer can handle all this work completely on its own, this saves the server a tremendous amount of work, cutting down on CPU and bandwidth usage.  Here is a schematic of what the new system looks like:

[URL=http://i.imgur.com/P7Khb9M.jpg][IMG]http://i.imgur.com/P7Khb9M.jpg[/IMG][/URL]

This is the system that Clark Fagot implemented for the game recently.  Red arrows increase load times and put load on the server, whereas green arrows load quickly and put no load on the server.


[h1]The Results[/h1]
[b][i]On average, it reduced the zone loading times for our players from 40 seconds to 8 seconds.[/i][/b]  This is the difference between getting bored and keeping the gameplay rolling.  In addition, it saves bandwidth for the game servers, and all the players.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[URL=https://forum.villagersandheroes.com/showthread.php?8361-Dev-Diary-quot-Geister-t%F6ten-Wie-wir-Zonenladezeiten-um-das-F%FCnffache-verk%FCrzt-haben-quot&p=69437#post69437]Geister töten, oder wie wir es geschafft haben, die Zonenladezeiten um das Fünffache zu verkürzen. [/URL]

notes.title: Monster Monday: Heartbruiser
notes.notes:
[i]Every Monday we release a new featured Bounty Boss, sharing a bit of lore and information about the Seven Realms most treacherous creatures. We are sharing our backlog of Monster Mondays for our Steam users to enjoy. [/i]

[IMG]http://i.imgur.com/r7zrDC8.png[/IMG]

[h1]Heartbruiser[/h1]
[b]Race:[/b] Ogre
[b]Location:[/b] Deforested Forest

Heartbruiser’s tale begins many years ago, during a time when Heartbruiser decided to seek a bit of adventure (or possibly ‘adventurers’, most likely to snack on. His intentions were vague). And so the Ogre left his dark gloomy cave and set out into the forests of Greenhaven. Being a slightly intelligent ogre, Heartbruiser had the foresight to mark his route on trees as he ventured deeper into the wild forests of Greenhaven.

After months of roaming, and finding several tasty wargs, daggertooths, as well as a few low level humans, Heartbruiser decided that the adventuring life was not for him, and headed home.

Shortly after beginning his return trip, Heartbruiser came upon a sad sight indeed, the deforested Forest. This wouldn’t have been particularly sad to Heartbruiser, or any ogre for that matter, unless of course those exact trees had been intentionally marked, which indeed they were. The treacherous goblins of Greenhaven had wiped clean Heartbruisers carefully marked path, the Ogre was now lost. In a fit of rage Heartbruiser stormed and rampaged through the first encampment he found, destroying any small green humanoid that smelled of oil and wood shavings. But eventually his rage slowed, his energy dwindled, and Heartbruiser had to face the cold truth that he would be forever lost in this terrible pit of dead trees and goblin odor.

And so Heartbruiser roams the deforested forest, angry, sad, and then angry some more, looking for any victim that he could use to vent out a few punches of frustration.

notes.title: Monster Monday: Bully Bacon
notes.notes:
[i]Every Monday we release a new featured Bounty Boss, sharing a bit of lore and information about the Seven Realms most treacherous creatures. We are sharing our backlog of Monster Mondays for our Steam users to enjoy. [/i]

[IMG]https://i.imgur.com/9YTHibH.png[/IMG]

[h1]Bully Bacon[/h1]
[b]Race:[/b] Boar
[b]Location:[/b] Elk Meadow

After moving to Ardent, Bully Bacon then became terribly aware of the vile nature of humans.

Every day thousands of humans would roll by his small nook of the city and simply kill him for sport. At first Bully Bacon thought this was because of all the experience that the humans were accumulating from their spars with him, but soon Bully Bacon realized a terrible truth… they weren’t. The amount of experience that humans were getting from him was negligible, and shortly after he realized that sometimes they would kill him simply hoping to find a piece of bacon to give some weirdo named Cyprian… times were bleak, and poor Bully Bacon hung his head in grief.

But then chance had it that King Leo decided to renovate the city, rebuilding it from the ground up. Bully Bacon came to realize that this was the perfect time for him to move back to the country. He packed up the few small things he owned, and in the midst of the chaos of construction, Bully slipped away.

With all of the experience of city life behind him, Bully Bacon grew in power, only a bit, but more than most bounty bosses ever do. He slipped into a quiet corner of Elk Meadow to live out his days. Of course he would still be killed on occasion, but these were much less frequent than before; overall Bully Bacon decided that he had found peace.

• 39 Milliarden Gold (38.805.979.859) wurde bisher von den Spielern zusammengezählt ausgegeben, um die Spielerdörfer zu verbessern, seit es Dorfprojekte gibt.

notes.title: Monster Monday: Leechwood
notes.notes:
[i]Every Monday we release a new featured Bounty Boss, sharing a bit of lore and information about the Seven Realms most treacherous creatures. We are sharing our backlog of Monster Mondays for our Steam users to enjoy. [/i]

[IMG]http://i.imgur.com/4gDmQhx.png[/iMG]

[h1]Leechwood[/h1]
[b]Race:[/b] Tree
[b]Location[/b] Maiden


When Maiden, infused with arcane magic’s broke from the snowy peaks of Stormhold, it caused quite the stir in much of the local fauna. And like most vegetation in Maiden, Leechwood absorbed a unique palette of magical qualities. 

The benefits of this magical imbuement were that he of course became strong and powerful, with a thick sturdy trunk, and deep growing roots.  His newly amassed branches were infused with strength, causing his boughs to swing with purpose and aim. His bark hardened, becoming impenetrable to all but the most skilled arrows and swords.

But as with most magic, there were some setbacks, the foremost being that most of his leaves fell off. While some might think that Leechwood was simply going through a season, the harsh truth was that Leechwood was now bald, something that he would be ridiculed greatly for through the whispers of the gossiping trees.

However the single most interesting thing that this magical concurrence performed on Leechwood, could be seen as a benefit, or a detriment; depending on the pondering party. Leechwood pulled his trunk from the ground for the first time, put one root in front of the other, and became what most people would call, alive.

notes.title: Class Builds: Fire Wizard
notes.notes:
[IMG]http://i.imgur.com/WnJ532R.jpg[/IMG]

[url=http://i.imgur.com/WnJ532R.jpg]Full Size Image[/url]

Hello Everyone, Diet here. 

Today we are going to get into the nitty gritty and talk about one of the many specs that a player can become, the Fire Wizard!

[h1]The Lore[/h1]
Fire Wizards, like all wizards, are students of their ancient elder, Calypso. Calypso was the first of their order, and master over both fire and ice. It was Calypso who first discovered how to weave the elements together, finding that the elements worked just as well side by side as they did against one another. Additionally, it was Calypso’s closest friend, the Sentinel Kalisar, who first discovered that the wizards could harness the powers of the physical plane, developing such spells as Spirit Orb, Strike, and Shockwave. The two of them together created most of the spells that modern day wizards so potently wield. 

[h1]Overview[/h1]
Wizards in general have several different ways they can specialize (spec). Wizards can spec pure Fire, pure Ice, Frostfire hybrid, Physical (aka the battle mage), or one of the many other variations. Each spec, just like all classes and build types, has its own set of strengths and weaknesses, the fire wizard being no exception.
Briefly, on the high level…

[h1]Fire Wizard Strengths:[/h1]
[list][*]High damage potential
[*]Large AOE damage (area of effect)
[*]Sustainable AOE crowd control (stuns)
[*]Excellent addition to parties and groups[/list]
[h1]Fire Wizard Weaknesses:[/h1]
[list][*]High spirit consumption
[*]Vulnerable in close range
[*]Not quite as adept at Solo play as other build types
[/list]
Fire Wizards have the potential for high burst damage with large amounts of AOE. In a group setup where a tank can pull a collection of mobs together, the fire wizard can absolutely decimate his or her foes. With long-ranged AOE spells (spells that have a radius dependent on the target rather than the caster), the fire wizard can stay out of harm’s way while dropping meteors and infernos onto the heads of their enemies. 

Additionally, with the use of skills like Fire Burst and Shockwave, fire wizards can stun groups of enemies that manage to close the gap and threaten the wizard’s position. With a well-timed fire burst matched with shockwave for backup, a smart fire wizard can almost always keep an enemy at bay.

And while fire wizards excel heavily at AOE damage, this doesn’t mean their single target damage suffers. With an entire arsenal of spells aimed at single targets, the fire wizard can let fly a lethal storm of scorching damage that will burn their foes to a crisp. 

The fire wizard does have a few drawbacks. The fast casting capability of the fire wizard often leaves them low on spirit. Some fire wizards choose to spec into Spirit Charm to help compensate, or possibly level up their skill in Cooking and Gardening so they can brew spirit regeneration potions. 

Additionally, with the low defenses of this build, the fire wizard does need to be careful how they select their battles. If a fire wizard goes into an area with spells-a-blazin’, they risk attracting too many enemies, and can be quickly overwhelmed. This is obviously is not a problem in a party or group situation, but in solo play the fire wizard does need to play smart, which sometimes can slow their pace. 

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Now to go into the details; I have gone through a few situations to give an idea how the fire wizard can be played. These of course are only the few of many different rotations, all dependent on player choice and play style. 

[h1]Casting Rotation:[i] Multiple Enemies[/i][/h1]
While fighting groups, the fire wizard wants to pull down as much chaos as possible, and as fast as possible. The faster the enemies fall, the safer the wizard becomes.

Leading the charge, I would suggest dropping a Flaming Meteor. This potent spell summons a meteor from the cosmos that lands in a molten blast on the enemy. The meteor explodes, dealing fire damage in a large radius and applying a burning damage over time effect to all enemy creatures hit.

Immediately after the meteor lands, you will have a swarming angry mass of enemies coming at you. Right on the heels of the meteor, throwing out an Inferno is a great way to get another hard AOE hit in.

Usually you can squeeze one more spell in before your enemies are on you. I like to pick one of the harder targets and throw out a Fireball. This ensures extra damage on the more dangerous targets.

At this point you will be surrounded by angry burning monsters, all of which want you as a dinner. This is where your Fire Burst spell comes in. Fire burst releases a ring of fire in a small radius surrounding you. As long as the enemies are within a reasonable level, your Fire Burst has 100% chance to stun the enemies for 7 seconds. This gives you ample time to finish off the baddies before they can finish off you.

If the enemy group happens to be a bit of a tougher group, shockwave can save your hide. Shockwave is the physical form of the Fire Burst (based on the research of the famous Sentinel Kalisar). Shockwave won’t do as much damage as your fire burst (since it isn’t augmented with fire damage), but it will have the same chance to stun, giving you some extra time to deal with your foes. 

After a shockwave cast, your inferno spell is probably ready to be cast again. Launch a final inferno to deal with whatever is left, and follow up with some single target spells like fireball or combust, to deal with the leftover. 

[h1]Casting Rotation: [i]Single Target[/i][/h1]
If you are facing a single, powerful foe, an optimal build and cast rotation can make the difference between life and death. 

Starting out, I would suggest Scorching Blast. This slow traveling spell takes a bit longer to reach its target, but has a powerful effect once it does. Scorching blast not only places a burning damage over time effect on the enemy, it also weakens the enemy against fire damage. That means that as soon as your scorching blast hits, every fire spell that hits that target will do extra fire damage!

As soon as your scorching blast ignites your target, follow up with a Fireball, and then a quick Combust. Fireball travels quickly, but as a missile does have a bit of travel time. Combust on the other hand is instant, as soon as the mystical runes are uttered from your lips, the enemy combusts in blazing fire. A well-timed Fireball and Combust, just on the heels of a Scorching Blast can absolutely obliterate your target. 

If after all that the enemy still manages to make its way to your location, a fire burst can halt them in their tracks, giving you ample time to launch another one-two punch combo with Fireball and Combust. 

For some added flavor, throw in a Spirit Orb on occasion. Spirit orb is a projectile orb of pure spirit pulled from its caster. While the spirit cost of Spirit Orb is extremely high, its damage is immense. Additionally, after your Spirit Orb blasts its target, the spirit fades into the nether, where you the Wizard can collect it again. A wizard can reclaim 80% of the spirit used to cast the orb over the course of 60 seconds. 

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
The fire wizard has a few weaknesses, but those are more than compensated for with their high damage potential, and quick-casting stun capability. The fire wizard is a great spec to try out on your wizard, and in general the wizard class is loads of fun. So what are you waiting for? Create a wizard and strut your stuff. Build them how you want to, and show us your build!

[h1]What you do is up to you. Who will you become?[/h1]
